decisions.reason: Mobile-friendly behavior is independent of the brand palette and positioning, and its existing same-message INTRODUCE already scopes that behavior to the master and location sites.

The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY for the clean, modern layout and visual composition. Brand colors and national positioning remain attributes of the separate brand-identity Requirement.
The brand-identity change does not alter the homepage information sections or their information goal; location selection is represented by the separate location-directory Requirement.
Consistent branding across locations does not entail any change to package catalogs or pricing.
The brand modification does not change location routing. The source message's separate selector and current-location clauses are already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
National brand positioning and cross-location visual consistency do not change the requirement to keep the legacy site available or linked during transition.

The candidate's existing same-message MODIFY already captures reuse of consistent SHATTER HOUSE branding across location pages and easy addition of future locations; no further update or removal is required.
The master-domain change is an independent clause already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; it is not a propagated consequence of the brand palette or positioning change.
The brand modification does not change which legacy content, images, or booking information must be reused.
Consistent customer-facing branding does not alter the separate placement and isolation of each location's booking operations.
The clarified brand palette and national positioning do not change the existing requirement to preserve SEO during the rebrand and migration.
Cross-location visual brand consistency does not change the requirement for location-specific analytics, revenue, sales, and reporting isolation.
